#2811. Drew Rosenhaus after Brandon Aiyuk's meeting with 49ers: "To be continued"

It has become abundantly clear that the NFL is delaying the reinstatement of 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list. It has also become abundantly clear that the 49ers hope to squeeze some cash out of Aiyuk before the league lets him back in.

It's no surprise, then, that Friday's sit-down between Aiyuk, agent Drew Rosenhaus, and the 49ers did not resolve the situation.

"Hey, guys," Rosenhaus told a group of reporters who had staked out the Friday meeting. "To be continued. We don't have any further statements right now. But when we do, we'll let you know."

The situation seems pretty simple. Aiyuk arguably owes the 49ers upwards of $13 million. It's one thing for the 49ers to have the ability to chase him around for the cash; it's another for the NFL and the 49ers to delay his reinstatement to the league until he wires the funds.

That seems to be precisely where things stand. And the question becomes whether Aiyuk will be willing to strike a deal with the 49ers in order to secure the ability to return to the NFL, with another team.

#2809. Ohio high school wins first playoff football game since 2016 after week-long saga

To say the last week has been lengthy for the University Preppers (OH) would be a massive understatement.

Despite committing no transgressions, the Preppers were embroiled in the controversy surrounding Glenville (OH) and the OHSAA after the organization banned the program from postseason play for using ineligible players.

Court cases ensued, judges made decisions, and University was left wondering who and when it would play its first postseason game. Thankfully, on Thursday, the program learned it would play Salem (OH) Friday night after an appeals court upheld the OHSAA's original decision.

Given the opportunity to play, the Preppers made the most out of it.

University beat Salem on the road Friday, 14-10, to advance to the Division III Region 9 regional semifinals. The win also marked a significant moment for the program as it was their first playoff win since 2016.

From initially refusing to play Glenville to not knowing whether that decision would cost them their season, the Preppers went into Friday leaning on a defense that struggled in their previous two games.

Early on, it looked like the Preppers would be in trouble as Salem jumped out to a 10-0 lead late in the first quarter. With just over six minutes remaining in the half, senior Tylar Robinson put the Preppers on the board with a 10-yard run.

That three-point deficit did not last long into the second half. Junior quarterback Nico Morelli connected with Robinson on a 60-yard touchdown pass just over a minute into the third quarter.

Salem had an opportunity late facing a fourth-and-goal situation deep inside University territory. However, they batted down the pass with 26 remaining to secure their long-awaited playoff win.

Now with this win out of the way, they can turn their attention to a Division III Region 9 regional semifinals road showdown with Ursuline on Nov. 13.

#2806. Lewis and Mallory help No. 9 Virginia overcome slow start and beat Northeastern

CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. (AP) — Sam Lewis and Chance Mallory each scored 20 points as No. 9 Virginia shrugged off a sluggish start and pulled away for a 97-72 win over Northeastern on Friday night.

Thijs De Ridder had 16 points, six rebounds and four assists, and Johann Grunloh, playing on an injured right ankle, added 13 points for the Cavaliers.

Rashad King scored 26 points and guard Louis Bond added 21 for the Huskies, who committed 19 turnovers.

With a matchup against No. 12 Arkansas on tap Sunday, Virginia (2-0) got off to a dreadful start, going 2 for 10 from the field, including 0 for 7 from 3-point range, and committing four turnovers in the first eight minutes.

Virginia didn't take its first lead until Mallory made a layup with 8:23 left in the half. The Cavaliers outscored the Huskies 22-11 over the final nine minutes of the half to take a 38-31 lead to the locker room. The two teams combined for 18 first-half turnovers, 11 by Northeastern.

But a dominant showing in the second half allowed Virginia to rest its starters for the final six minutes. That figures to be important, considering the Cavaliers are getting the bulk of their scoring from the four key players they retained from last year's 30-win squad.

BOSTON )AP) — Braylon Mullins scored 23 points and connected on 10 of 11 free throws to help UConn beat Michigan in a rematch of last season's NCAA championship game.

Silas Demary Jr. finished with 21 points and seven rebounds. Colben Landrew added 14 points and eight rebounds off the bench for the Huskies (2-0) at TD Garden, home to the Boston Celtics.

Michigan (1-1) got within single digits in the final minute, but the Huskies closed it out at the foul line.

In last season's title game, the Wolverines held off UConn 69-63 despite making only two 3-pointers.

This time, Michigan again struggled from beyond the arc, going 7 of 28. But the Wolverines couldn't keep up with a Huskies team that led by 18 in the first half. UConn connected on nine 3s and shot 42% from the field overall, compared to 41% by Michigan.

CORAL GABLES, Fla. (AP) — Shelton Henderson scored 19 points and Miami rebounded from a season-opening loss against top-ranked Florida to beat Wagner.

Malik Reneau finished with 12 points and Caleb Gaskins added 11 for the Hurricanes (1-1), who outscored Wagner 24-3 in fast-break points and had 18 assists. Miami made 16 of 18 free throws and had a 52-22 advantage in the paint.

Reneau averaged a team-leading 18 points last season while Henderson scored 13 per game but both struggled in the opener Monday against Florida, finishing with five and seven, respectively.

After a second-chance layup by Tajae Jones gave the Seahawks their only lead at 10-8 in the opening four minutes, the Hurricanes responded with a 22-4 run.

Gaskins, Brent Bland and Nick Dorn hit 3-pointers to key the surge. Dante Allen's layup with 4:35 capped the spurt and put Miami ahead 30-14.

LAWRENCE, Kan. (AP) — Trey Kaufman-Renn scored 17 points in 18 minutes and led Kansas to a rout of Middle Tennessee.

Kaufman-Renn, a fifth-year senior who transferred from Purdue, shot 7 for 8 from the field and grabbed four rebounds. Through two games with Kansas (2-0), he is 11 for 13 from the field.

His efficiency helped pace the Jayhawks, who shot a blistering 63% in the game while holding Middle Tennessee to just 25%.

Fifth-year center Christian Reeves added 10 points for Kansas.

The Jayhawks were particularly effective in the paint, using their size to outscore the Blue Raiders 48-16. They also pulled down 32 defensive rebounds to limit second chances.

The Kansas bench chipped in 46 points to help keep Middle Tennessee at bay and build the lead to as many as 50 points in the second half.

AMES, Iowa (AP) — Tre Singleton scored 19 of his career-high 28 points in the first half to lead Iowa State past Southern Mississippi.

The Cyclones (1-1), who lost their opener to Memphis on a neutral court Monday, have won nine straight home openers and 25 of their last 26.

Iowa State dominated inside in the first half, outscoring the Golden Eagles 26-6 in the paint while jumping out to a 46-29 halftime lead.

The Cyclones took a double-digit lead late in the first half on Dominykas Pleta's fast-break dunk, and they were up by 29 in the middle of the first half.

Iowa State coach T.J. Otzelberger played nine players, and all of them got at least 10 minutes and scored. The Cyclones finished with a 42-20 advantage in the paint and converted Southern Miss' 18 turnovers into 23 points.

Singleton, who transferred from Northwestern, shot 7 of 9 from the field in the first half and 10 of 17 for the game. He also had a team-high nine rebounds.

Jaquan Johnson had 10 points and four assists for the Cyclones.

TUSCALOOSA, Ala. (AP) — Amari Allen had 16 points, 13 rebounds and 11 assists for the fifth triple-double in program history as Alabama beat Arkansas State.

Allen got his 10th assist on Brandon Garrison's layup with just over six minutes left. Before the final media timeout, Allen landed awkwardly, grabbed his right ankle and needed help off the floor. He returned to the bench after the timeout. Arkansas State's Amadou Doumbia went straight to the locker room after he was also slow to get up.

Alabama guard Aden Holloway served the final game of a five-game suspension following his March arrest on drug charges that were later dismissed. Freshman forward Jaxon Richardson sat out with an upper-body injury.

Layne Taylor made his first three 3-point shots to help Arkansas State (1-1) take a 19-11 lead. He finished with 20 points and six assists. Chaz Watson added 15 points and Doumbia had 11 points and 10 rebounds.

LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — Zoom Diallo and Alex Wilkins each scored 16 points to lead Kentucky to a win over James Madison.

The Wildcats (2-0) overcame 18 lead changes and five ties before pulling way with a 15-3 run that turned a 56-54 deficit into a 69-59 lead with 10 minutes remaining.

Former James Madison forward Justin McBride added 13 points, Mason Williams had 12 and Brayden Hawthorne 10 for Kentucky. Milan Momcilovic (24 points per game) scored just seven points.

Diallo scored 10 points in the first half, including six during a 9-0 run. Kentucky finished with 10 3-pointers, including three by McBride.

The Dukes (0-2) made 15 3-pointers, including nine in the first half to keep the game within reach.

Brandon Lee led James Madison (0-2) with 26 points. Garrett Sundra added 15 points and Paul Jones III 12 for the Dukes.

#2804. MLB qualifying offer: Predicting who will get a QO this offseason, plus how the $23.15 million contract works

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Milwaukee Brewers have been crowned the 2026 World Series champions and the 2026-27 offseason is already underway. More than 100 players became free agents the day after the World Series ended, and soon teams will have to make decisions about contract options and qualifying offers.

The qualifying offer (QO) entitles teams to draft-pick compensation in the event that they lose a free agent to another team. The QO is a one-year deal set at the average of the top 125 salaries in baseball. This offseason, it's worth a record $23.15 million, according to the New York Post. That is up from $22.025 million last year, $21.05 million the year before, and $20.325 million the year before that.

Teams have until five days after the end of the World Series to tender their free agents the QO, and players who receive it then have until 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 17 to accept or reject. Players who accept the QO remain with their team and cannot be traded without their consent until June 15. Players who reject the QO become free agents with draft-pick compensation attached.

Simple, right? The process is, but the decisions aren't always. With that in mind, let's run down this offseason's QO candidates, as well as explain the draft-pick compensation rules.

Yes, the QO is still a thing this offseason. The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and the next CBA could change the QO rules, maybe even eliminate it entirely. That said, until that happens, the QO remains in place. Decisions to tender the QO (made by the team) and decisions to accept or reject the QO (made by the player) are due before the CBA expires.

Once upon a time, teams that lost an eligible free agent received a compensation draft pick after the first round. It was nice and easy. The current rules are a bit more complicated. Here are compensation rules for teams that lose a qualified free agent:

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round)

Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round)

The Athletics, Brewers, Cardinals, Diamondbacks, Guardians, Mariners, Marlins, Orioles, Pirates, Rays, Reds, Rockies, Royals, Tigers, and Twins received revenue sharing this season, so the first two scenarios apply to them. The Blue Jays, Braves, Cubs, Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Phillies, Red Sox, and Yankees will pay competitive balance tax (CBT), so they're in the third scenario. The Angels, Astros, Giants, Nationals, Rangers, and White Sox neither received revenue sharing nor paid CBT. They're in the fourth bucket.

Now here are the penalties for signing a qualified free agent:

The Blue Jays, Braves, Cubs, Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Phillies, Red Sox, and Yankees will pay CBT and are in the first group. The Athletics, Brewers, Cardinals, Diamondbacks, Guardians, Mariners, Marlins, Orioles, Pirates, Rays, Reds, Rockies, Royals, Tigers, and Twins received revenue sharing and are in the second group. The Angels, Astros, Giants, Nationals, Rangers, and White Sox are the third group. Got it? Good.

Thirteen players received the QO last offseason: Trent Grisham, Shota Imanaga, Gleyber Torres, and Brandon Woodruff accepted the QO; Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber declined but signed new contracts to remain with their teams; Bo Bichette, Dylan Cease, Edwin Díaz, Kyle Tucker, Ranger Suárez, and Framber Valdez rejected the QO and signed with new teams, giving their former clubs compensatory draft picks. Teams do not gain or lose draft picks for re-signing their own qualified free agent.

Players are eligible for the QO as long as they spent the entire 2026 season with one team and did not receive the QO previously. That means several high-profile free agents are not eligible for the QO this offseason. Here are the notables:

CHANGED TEAMS Luis Arraez Kevin Gausman (also received QO previously) Casey Mize Freddy Peralta Tarik Skubal Daulton Varsho

PREVIOUSLY RECEIVED QO Bo Bichette (opt out) Sonny Gray (mutual option) Michael King (opt out)  Nick Martinez

The Tigers traded Skubal, the reigning two-time AL Cy Young winner, to the Dodgers for a three-prospect package at the deadline. MLB Pipeline currently ranks those players as Detroit's No. 1 (Zyhir Hope), No. 3 (River Ryan), and No. 9 (Brady Smith) prospects. That's a much better haul than the compensation draft pick the Tigers would have received had they kept Skubal all year and made him the QO. Anyway, these free agents are among those not eligible for the QO this offseason.

This is not the best free agent class and, as a result, I count only two stone-cold locks to receive a QO: Randy Arozarena (Mariners) and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs). The Mariners and Cubs would be thrilled if Arozarena and Seiya accepted the QO and returned next season on one-year contracts that aren't too much of a raise. Arozarena made $15.65 million this year. Suzuki earned $18 million. The jump to $23.15 million isn't big enough to shy away from the QO, plus these are really good players. Arozarena and Suzuki will receive the QO and decline it.

Although Arozarena and Suzuki are the only locks to get the QO, in my opinion, there are three other free agents-to-be who seem like pretty good bets to receive it. Here are those three players:

Ryan Jeffers, Twins: Jeffers will be the best catcher to hit the open market since Willson Contreras four years ago. He missed time with a hamate injury this year and his defense isn't great, plus he'll turn 30 next June. Those seem like nitpicks compared to the offense he brings to the table at the catcher position. The only reason I don't think Jeffers is a lock to get the QO is the fact that the Twins have shaved roughly $50 million off their payroll the last four years. They might get thrifty.

Brandon Lowe, Pirates: Pittsburgh knocked it out of the park with the Mike Burrows-for-Lowe-and-Mason Montgomery three-team trade with the Astros and Rays. Montgomery is a bullpen ace and Lowe slugged 35 home runs, the most by a Pirate since Josh Bell hit 37 in 2019. Lowe's age (32), poor contact rates, and history of poor defense (though not in 2026) create collapse risk. Also, the Pirates run a bottom 10 payroll every season. I expect Lowe to get the QO. I just wouldn't be surprised if the Pirates decide not to risk him taking it, thereby soaking up 20% or so of their 2027 payroll.

Trevor Rogers, Orioles: Rogers, 29 in November, was a bright spot in an otherwise lost season for the O's. He stayed healthy and threw a career-high 169 ⅔ innings, and pitched exceptionally well after June 1: 2.90 ERA with under-the-hood numbers to match (2.89 FIP and 3.10 expected ERA). Rogers might be the second-best free agent starter behind Skubal given his success the last two years and (more importantly) analytically friendly arsenal. During the president of baseball operations Mike Elias era, the Orioles haven't always done the most sensible thing when it comes to spending money. I think it's 99% certain the O's will give Rogers the QO, but 99% is not 100%.

My hunch is teams will be conservative with their QO decisions this offseason because a new CBA is coming, and no one knows what the game's economic landscape will look like next year. Will there be a salary cap? More punitive CBT penalties? I would expect teams to err on the side of caution when it comes to potentially committing $23.15 million to one player. Even a good player they may want back, but not necessarily at $23.15 million in 2027. Here are three borderline QO cases:

David Bednar, Yankees: Bednar has proven he can close games in New York, which is not nothing, but he did just turn 32, and the $23.15 million QO would make him the highest-paid reliever in baseball. I think the Yankees want to bring Bednar back next season. Enough to risk him accepting the QO? When the potential reward is a dinky draft pick after the fourth round given their CBT status? That I'm not sold on. A multi-year contract at a lower annual salary is the much more likely path to Bednar returning to the Yankees.

Jazz Chisholm Jr., Yankees: Even in a down year, Chisholm was a 3.5-WAR player thanks to the breadth of his skill set. He hit 19 homers, he stole 41 bases, and he was fourth among second basemen with +13 outs above average. The all-around game and the fact that Chisholm will play the entire 2027 season at age 29 would seem to make him a slam dunk QO candidate. My sense is the Yankees won't commit any significant payroll to next season without first seeing what the new CBA brings, which is exactly what they did before the last lockout. I think the Yankees value the payroll flexibility (i.e. the certainty that Chisholm won't take the QO) more than the post-fourth round compensation pick they would receive if he signed elsewhere.

Adrian Morejon, Padres: Morejon will be an interesting test case for San Diego's new ownership. He is outstanding, one of the five or six best relievers in baseball, and he'll play the entire 2027 season at age 28. The QO would make Morejon the highest-paid reliever in the game, but only if he takes it, and his age and effectiveness would seem to make that unlikely. Do the Padres roll the dice and give Morejon the QO, and risk sinking $23.15 million into a (great) setup man, or not bother because they're only in line to receive a draft pick after the fourth round if he leaves? Díaz, Josh Hader (from the Padres), and Raisel Iglesias are the only relievers to get the QO in the last seven years. Is Morejon in that class?

#2802. No. 12 Sun Valley Poly earns City Section Division I upset over No. 5 Marshall

Talk about strange beginnings at Friday's City Section Division I football playoff opener between Sun Valley Poly and host Marshall.

After the opening kickoff went into the end zone for a touchback, Poly coach Boo Williams immediately called a timeout when he saw his double-wing offense lining up with 12 players. After a discussion, the next play was an illegal procedure penalty on the Parrots.

Looking confused, the Parrots deserved an Academy Award for their acting skills, because on their third play, quarterback King Exusdus took the snap from shotgun formation and sprinted 82 yards for a touchdown.

Marshall, seeded No. 5 after its first 10-0 regular season in school history, never figured out how to slow down the Parrots' run-oriented attack and couldn't overcome a sore shoulder that limited quarterback Nathaniel Cadet's ability to pass in a 20-0 loss to 12th-seeded Poly (10-1).

"Who says Poly can't win a Division I playoff game?" Williams said.

With each short pass in pregame warmups, Cadet grabbed his right shoulder as if he were in pain — and he was. On Saturday, he couldn't move his arm because of a contusion and sprain to his AC shoulder joint suffered in the regular-season finale last week against Eagle Rock.

All week, Cadet alternated between applying ice and heat to his shoulder. He looked at Instagram and found a shoulder sleeve designed to provide support. He took four Advil tablets. The Barristers badly needed him. He came in with 1,570 yards passing and 24 touchdowns, but on his second pass of the game, he came to the sideline in severe pain revealing the challenge he was facing. He ended up passing for just 55 yards and was intercepted twice.

For Poly — the East Valley League champions under Williams in his first year as coach — the turnaround from a football program with little history of success to competing in City Division I has been meteoric. After problems at the start of the game and a few illegal procedure penalties, the Parrots ran the double wing to perfection, with 290-pound lineman Diego Rodriguez clearing a path like he was knocking down pins with a bowling ball.

Exusdus, usually a receiver, finished with 174 yards rushing in 13 carries. Justice Brown rushed for 86 yards and caught Poly's only pass, a 26-yard touchdown on fourth down from quarterback Alijah Ochoa.

"One pass, one touchdown, baby," former Sylmar All-City quarterback Clarence Williams said. He's the quarterback coach at Poly.

On defense, linebacker Stephon Boyd was all over the field making tackles. Exusdus and Boyd used to attend Birmingham before arriving at Poly this season.

Exusdus is grateful just to be out on the field. He missed all last season attending a continuation school as he tried to improve a grade-point average that he said was once below 1.0. Playing football in his senior year made him start showing up on time to practices and making progress in the classroom.

"I had to get everything right," he said. "It motivated me. Seeing friends go Division I fueled me."

It was a difficult ending for a Marshall team that won the Northern League title and had not won a Division I playoff game since 2000. Poly moves on to the quarterfinals and will face either Chatsworth or Banning.

#2801. MLB rumors: Mets' Bo Bichette makes contract decision, familiar All-Star back on trade block

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is only two days old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and here are the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

As expected, Mets infielder Bo Bichette has picked up his $42 million player option for 2027, reports The Athletic. He holds another $42 million player option for 2028. Still only 28, Bichette had a poor first season in Queens, posting a .702 OPS with 18 home runs while showing growing pains as he transitioned from shortstop over to third base.

For now, the Mets are set on the infield with Bichette at third, Francisco Lindor at short, and Marcus Semien at second. They must figure out first base, and it is possible they will make a trade to shake up that veteran infield. Moving Semien would be ideal, but it may not be doable. Lindor's name figures to pop up in trade rumors against this offseason.

The Diamondbacks are expected to listen to offers for second baseman Ketel Marte, reports the Arizona Republic. The D-backs entertained trade offers last offseason, but were unable to find a match. Marte has full no-trade protection and can direct where he lands, if he wants to leave Arizona at all. His desire to change teams is unknown.

Marte, 33, had a down year by his standards in 2026. He also went AWOL in August, prompting the D-backs to put him on the restricted list. Manager Torey Lovullo later revealed it was the fourth straight season Marte missed a game without permission. Beyond the on-field fit, teams will have to weigh the potential clubhouse impact and headaches.

The Seibu Lions in Japan will make right-hander Kaima Taira available to MLB teams via the posting system this offseason, the team announced Friday. The posting is expected to be made official in the coming days. Once that happens, Taira will have 45 days to negotiate and sign with an MLB team, otherwise he will return to Japan in 2027.

We ranked Taira as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason. Here's our write-up:

Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man.

Taira, 27 next month, threw 146 innings with a 1.36 ERA and 141 strikeouts this past season. He actually had higher ERAs as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, though he has been excellent throughout his career in Japan, and has the bat-missing power stuff that tends to translate well to MLB. Taira figures to be highly sought after in the coming weeks.

The trading season resumed Thursday and the Red Sox were involved in the offseason's first two trades. First, they sent utility man Nate Eaton to the Athletics for minor-league righty Jareth Rayo, the team announced. The A's recently named former Red Sox assistant general manager Taylor Smith their new president of baseball operations. His first move was bringing in Eaton, a player he's presumably familiar with given their overlapping time in Boston.

Next, the Red Sox traded infielder Tsung-Che Cheng to the Tigers for cash, the team announced. Cheng, 25, is a glove-first utility man who appeared in 14 games with Boston this past season. Both the Cheng and Eaton trades open up 40-man roster spots for the Red Sox, who still must open three more spots to accommodate their seven players on the 60-day injured list. They must be activated no later than this coming Monday.

#2800. Shelby efficient in all facets in regional quarterfinal football win

SHELBY — The Shelby Whippets fumbled on the very first play, but from then on, it was perfection.

The slight hiccup was quickly erased as they cruised to a 42-3 Division IV Region 14 quarterfinal victory over Firelands on Friday, Nov. 6 and will host Perkins (11-0) on Nov. 13 in the regional semifinals.

The Whippets were efficient in ever sense of the word on offense scoring 14 points in the first quarter and 21 in the second to build a 35-3 lead at the half and start the second half with a running clock.

ONTARIO WINS: Ontario finds a way to win in regional quarterfinal victory over Columbian

Michael Shepherd hit Brady Bowman for a 47-yard touchdown to open the scoring before Shepherd added a 1-yard TD run to close out the first quarter. Gavin Baker added a 1-yard TD run, Casyn Koch caught a 15-yard touchdown from Shepherd and Baker added his second TD of the night from five yards out all in the second quarter to build the insurmountable advantage. Shepherd added an 11-yard TD run in the third quarter for good measure.

"Other than the fumble on the first play, I thought we were pretty dang efficient," Shelby coach Rob Mahaney told Marc Hartz of the Shelby Daily Globe. "That is what we want to be. There will be games where we throw for 400 or run for 400, but we want to pride ourselves to take what the defense gives us and our kids did a great job of that tonight. We sustained drives and that will be huge for us next week against Perkins."

The Whippets (11-0) ran for 237 yards on 25 carries led by Baker's 115-yard, 2-touchdown performance. Like Blevins added 49 yards while Brady Bowman had 44 and Shepherd had 31 with a pair of scores.

"If we are going to do well in the postseason, it is going to fall on those guys up front," Mahaney said. "Those senior offensive linemen did a great job for us tonight and Michael (Shepherd) was great in the read game. The backs ran hard and our senior tight end Max Miller did a great job blocking, too. Brady running the jets. In high school football, you have to find a way to run the ball especially in the playoffs."

After spending last week resting up with a week off thanks to earning a Top 4 seed in the Region 14 playoffs, the Whippets ran with fresh legs and it showed.

"To come off of the bye week and run like that, I am very proud of our guys," Mahaney said. "It got us to find a way to next week."

Shepherd completed 8-of-10 passes for 128 yards and two TDs while Bowman caught five passes for 90 yards and a score and Koch had 21 yards with a TD.

Defensively, the Whippets were insanely good yet again. Firelands ran for negative-7 yards on 11 carries, but did complete 19-of-39 passes for 220 yards. The ability to stop the run was huge for Shelby.

"Our defense played a great game," Mahaney said. "Coming into the season, our defense was a question mark, but through 11 games, our run defense has been amazing. Our D-line controls the line of scrimmage and Gavin Garrett and Bryce Booker do a great job in the middle. Our edge guys get penetration and our linebackers fly around. It has been awesome to see and they make offenses one dimensional."

Now, the Whippets move on to host Perkins in a highly-anticipated regional semifinal game after the Pirates beat Bellevue 42-14 in a quarterfinal matchup. It will be the first matchup between the two teams since 1979.

"All offseason, we thought if we wanted a chance to win the region, it would go through Perkins at some point," Mahaney said. "Now, we get to see that. You look at the success out of this region over the last two years and it is us and them. This is why you play high school football. To play a game with two 11-0 teams and a chance to play for a regional championship is all you could ask for."

This article originally appeared on Mansfield News Journal: Shelby efficient in all facets in regional quarterfinal football win

#2798. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2793. Ravens finalize Jacoby Brissett trade, swap Day 3 picks with Cardinals

The Baltimore Ravens have completed their trade with the Arizona Cardinals to acquire veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The terms are as follows, per ESPN's Adam Schefter:

Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett, 2027 fifth-round pick

Cardinals receive: 2027 fourth- and 2028 seventh-round picks

Arizona restructured Brissett's deal before finalizing the deal, so the Ravens will owe him $2.4 million, though Russell Street Report's Brian McFarland notes some of that money could be pushed into 2027.

To clear a spot on their active roster, the Ravens waived quarterback Austin Reed, who served as Joe Fagnano's backup on Thursday night against the Jaguars but did not play a snap. He could end up back on Baltimore's practice squad as additional quarterback insurance.

Brissett will get to work learning Declan Doyle's offense in preparation for a Week 10 matchup against the currently-winless Los Angeles Chargers. The 10-year veteran will make his Ravens debut on Monday Night Football – certainly a storyline that ESPN's producers were not expecting to push when the NFL set the primetime schedule.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Philadelphia opened the season with a 7-0 loss to the rival Pittsburgh Penguins, and coach Rick Tocchet described his team's play as "disturbing." There was only one way for the season to go after that, right? Wrong.

The Flyers are off to an 0-2-2 start, and the underlying numbers aren't pretty. Per Natural Stat Trick, they have a five-on-five expected goals share of 26.0%, which ranks last in the NHL. Their 4.57 xGA/60 also ranks last. Their 1.94 xGF/60? You guessed it. Last.

Tocchet's bunch entered the season with a lot of well-earned optimism. Even with subpar play from Matvei Michkov last season, the Flyers managed to reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2788. Astros hire Randy Flores as new general manager as offseason filled with questions begins in Houston

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Houston Astros' search for a new head of baseball operations has ended with the hiring of Randy Flores as general manager. The 51-year-old Flores had been an assistant general manager with the St. Louis Cardinals. In Houston, Flores replaces Dana Brown, who was let go in late August. Flores becomes the fourth head of baseball operations to serve under Astros owner Jim Crane.

"Randy has had a huge impact on the Cardinals over the last 10 seasons," Crane said in a statement released by the club. "Throughout the entire interview process, we've been thoroughly impressed with Randy and his background in scouting and player acquisition. We're happy to welcome Randy and his family to the Astros and we can't wait to get to work on bringing another championship to Houston."

Added Flores: "I am excited and grateful for this amazing opportunity. The Astros have a long winning tradition under Jim Crane, and I look forward to contributing to the success.  I want to thank the Cardinals organization for the opportunities and support that made this next chapter possible. My family and I are excited to make Houston home."

Flores for roughly a decade served as scouting director for the Cardinals and was tasked with running their draft. He added the assistant GM title in 2018 and saw his portfolio of responsibilities expand within the last year.

Flores takes over an Astros organization beset by uncertainty. With an aging roster and after several key departures over the years, the Astros have seen their season-long win total decline for four straight years. This past season, the Astros eked out the American League Central title but finished with a .500 record and a negative run differential. In terms of success and roster strength, they're a long way from their dynasty years of 2017-22. It's not certain whether the Astros moving forward will try to squeeze out another season of relevance or embrace a rebuild, but either path will have its challenges.

Speaking of challenges, Crane and his trusted advisor Jeff Bagwell have been an increasingly meddlesome presence in recent years, and it's unclear to what degree Flores will have autonomy in his role. Whatever the future holds, Flores' first major decision is filling the managerial vacancy. After the end of the regular season, Crane opted not to renew the contract of former manager Joe Espada.

Prior to beginning his front office career, Flores spent parts of eight seasons in the majors as a left-handed reliever. In 2006, he earned a World Series ring as a member of that Cardinals team.

#2786. "It's going to be amazing" – Campbell on Dortmund return

Signal Iduna Park was home for Cole Campbell for four years, but on Saturday, the American will be on the opposite side. The forward left Borussia Dortmund for newly-promoted Elversberg in the summer, where he has hit the ground running.

"I’ve had confidence in what I can do, and I am very grateful that Elversberg has put the trust in me and given me the confidence back," said Campbell in an interview with the DFL. "It’s been amazing to be here and to feel the trust and confidence that they have in me, so I am very happy to be here."

Campbell scored his first Bundesliga goal in Elversberg's opener, a surprise 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen. Since then, he's been moved to more of a bench role, partially due to injuries and partially to the emergence of other Elversberg attackers, like Maurice Krattenmacher.

Still, Campbell has made an impact when he's played. He scored with an acrobatic kick against Mainz to clinch a 4-1 win, taking Elversberg up to seventh in the Bundesliga. It was just his second top-flight goal.

“It was an amazing feeling for me to score a goal like this,” said Campbell. "I was very happy after the game and was also happy to have helped the team secure the win."

Campbell was only 18 when he made his debut in the Champions League, coming off the bench in front of a packed stadium against Sturm Graz. He replaced Jamie Gittens as Dortmund, then led by Nuri Şahin, snatched a dramatic 1-0 win at the death.

“At that point, it was probably one of my best feelings, and it was a dream come true to make my debut in the Champions League,” said Campbell. "To play in the Signal Iduna Park was also a different feeling, and I am really looking forward to getting to play there again this weekend. It was an amazing feeling for me.”

After four years and just seven appearances, Campbell left Dortmund in search of minutes. He joined Hoffenheim on loan last January, but injuries limited him to only five appearances. He was an unused substitute when Hoffenheim took on Dortmund in April.

That is unlikely to be the case this season. With the exception of the Augsburg match, which he missed because of an injury, Campbell has played every match this season for Elversberg. Even if he doesn't start, it's still likely he comes off the bench for a reunion with Niko Kovač's Borussia Dortmund and Signal Iduna Park.

“It’s a lot of emotions, and it will be very weird to be there and to not be in a Dortmund jersey,” said Campbell. "I am really looking forward to it, and I am very excited to see my friends and old teammates. I think it will be a special moment for me.”

Campbell debuted for the United States national team in October, coming off the bench in a 1-0 win over Canada.

The winger was also eligible for Iceland through his mother's side, initially playing there at youth level. While he's committed to the United States, Campbell takes the influence of both countries with him.

“It’s a mix of both,” said Campbell in an interview with the DFL. "I would say I take a little bit of both, but I feel more at home in the US for sure.”

Campbell was born in Houston, Texas, but his mother was part of the Iceland national team. He moved to Iceland at a young age, and when he was 15, Campbell was playing in Iceland's top flight. He stayed in the country for two years before leaving for Borussia Dortmund.

“I would say I feel more American, but I also like certain parts of Iceland, and a lot of my friends are from there,” said Campbell. “My mom, my grandma, and lots of my family are from there, so I love to go back there to visit."

#2784. MLB rumors: Padres decline option on key rotation piece, Korean star to be posted

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is only four days old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and here are the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Sunday's hot stove happenings.

San Diego's top two starters are now free agents. Two days after Michael King exercised an opt-out clause to become a free agent, the Padres declined their $14 million club option on Nick Pivetta, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Had the Padres picked up the option, Pivetta would have held an $18 million player option for 2028. That surely factored into the team's decision.

Pivetta, 34 in February, missed roughly five months with a flexor strain this past season. He returned late in the season and pitched reasonably well in six starts spanning September and the postseason. The San Diego Union-Tribune notes the Padres still have concerns about Pivetta's elbow, but could re-sign him to a new contract with a lower salary and/or no player option.

San Diego signed Pivetta to what amounted to a two-year, $23 million contact with two players options in February 2025. The flexor strain triggered an injury clause that converted the 2027 player option into a club option. We ranked Pivetta as the offseason's 43rd-best free agent.

As expected, the Orioles have declined their $20 million club option for center fielder Luis Robert Jr., reports ESPN. They will pay him a $2 million buyout, so it was functionally an $18 million decision. Robert suffered a hamstring injury and played only three games with the O's after being claimed off waivers from the Mets in late September.

Now 29, Robert again had multiple stints on the injured list this past season. He continued to punish lefties and play solid center field defense when healthy, but injuries have limited him to only 271 of 489 possible regular-season games from 2024-26. We did not rank Robert among our top 50 free agents, though he is an interesting upside play given his age.

The Hanwha Eagles of the Korea Baseball Organization will post star third baseman Si-Hwan Roh for MLB teams this offseason, reports Yonhap News Agency. Roh signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and $23 million), though as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the team once his MLB stint is over.

Roh, 26, has been one of the KBO's best players the last several years. He hit .283/.360/.505 with 29 home runs in 2026, and has averaged 35 home runs per 162 games since 2023. Roh is considered a reliable but unspectacular defender at third, plus he has first base experience as well. This free agent class is very thin at the hot corner. Roh should generate a good deal of interest.

KBO players get a 30-day negotiating window once officially posted. If Roh does not sign with an MLB team during the 30-day window, he will return to the Eagles. It's possible that Roh, a right-handed hitter, will eclipse his $23 million guarantee with the Eagles over just a handful of years with an MLB team.

The Astros have acquired Triple-A righty reliever Evan Reifert from the Rays for cash, reports the Tampa Bay Times. Houston is likely to add him to their 40-man roster to protect him from the Rule 5 Draft. The Rays did not have the roster space to do that, so they traded for cash rather than lose him for nothing. Reifert, 27, has an excellent slider and used it to strike out 81 batters in 58 Triple-A innings in 2026. He should spend time in Houston's bullpen next season.

Pittsburgh has always been home, and I'm proud to give back to a city that means so much to me."

Kuntz is in his sixth season with the Steelers. He has played in 93 games and counting in his career. Kuntz grew up in the Pittsburgh area, attending Chartiers Valley High School in Bridgeville, Pennsylvania. The long snapper played college ball at Duquesne, where he still holds the program's career sack record. The hometown kid is making a big impact in the place he has always called home.

#2782. ‘Slumping‘: Skip Bayless fires shots at LeBron James after 76ers are 'blown out' by the Cavs

The Philadelphia 76ers have just suffered a 119-95 defeat against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

All eyes ahead of the game were on LeBron James on his return to Cleveland, and he received a warm welcome from the home fans when his name was announced in the arena as well.

However, on the floor, things did not go James' way as the Sixers, shockingly, ended up losing by 24 points.

Nobody really expected the 76ers to lose to the Cavs on Friday night, especially by a staggering 24-point margin.

The Sixers went into the game with an 8-1 record and had looked incredible in most of their previous games. They had become many people's favourites to win the championship this season.

However, the defeat against the Cavaliers showed that it may not be as straightforward after all, as Philly looked nothing like their usual selves.

Bayless, as he always does, reacted to the game right after the final buzzer, and he fired a few shots at James for his performance.

He tweeted: "Sixers shockingly blown out in LeBron's return to Cleveland. Nobody could make a shot but LeBron (8 pts/6 turnovers), again slumping from 3.

"Last season 31.7 per cent, 3rd worst in the NBA. This year 22 per cent (6-27 after 0-4 tonight). LeBricks!"

#2781. Mets legend Jerry Koosman dies at 83: Pitcher helped New York win 1969 World Series

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Mets team Hall of Famer and two-time All-Star Jerry Koosman died Sunday morning in Osceola, Wisconsin, the team announced. He was 83. The Mets say Koosman battled multiple illnesses before his death.

"Kooz was one of the greatest pitchers in team history and a beloved member of the Mets family," Mets owners Alex and Steve Cohen said in a statement. "The 1969 Miracle Mets were filled with heroes, and the special southpaw from Appleton, Minnesota, was central to their success. He was a fierce competitor on the field, and respected teammate in the clubhouse. His legendary performance in the World Series helped the Mets secure their first Championship in team history. On behalf of the entire Mets organization, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Jerry's family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him."

The Mets discovered Koosman while he was pitching for the United States Army and signed him to a contract in August 1964. He made his MLB debut in April 1967 and moved into the rotation full-time the next season. Koosman threw 263 ⅔ innings with a 2.08 ERA as a rookie in 1968, which earned him an All-Star Game selection and MVP votes, and a second-place finish in the Rookie of the Year voting behind Hall of Famer Johnny Bench.

In 1969, Koosman was again an All-Star, throwing 241 innings with a 2.28 ERA. He was New York's No. 2 starter in the postseason between Hall of Famers Tom Seaver and Nolan Ryan. Koosman made two starts for the Miracle Mets in the World Series, including the Game 5 clincher against the Baltimore Orioles. He allowed three runs in the complete game win and recorded all but one possible out in his two World Series starts.

From 1968-76, Koosman was simply one of the best pitchers in the game, pitching to a 2.94 ERA and averaging 223 innings per season. The Mets traded him to the Minnesota Twins for Jesse Orosco in December 1978 and Koosman finished his career with stints for the Twins (1979-81), Chicago White Sox (1981-83), and Philadelphia Phillies (1984-85).

Koosman retired following the 1985 season with a 222-209 record and a 3.36 ERA that is 39th among AL/NL pitchers with at least 3,500 career innings. He ranks 35th all-time in strikeouts (2,556), 40th all-time in starts (527), 48th all-time in innings (3,839 ⅓), and 77th all-time in pitching WAR (57.0). Koosman went to two All-Star Games and finished second to Randy Jones in the 1976 Cy Young voting.

The Mets inducted Koosman into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his No. 36 in 2021. His 140 wins are the most in franchise history among left-handers and third in team history overall, behind Seaver (198) and Dwight Gooden (157). Koosman is second in Mets history in innings (behind Seaver) and third in strikeouts (behind Seaver and Gooden).

Koosman fell off the Baseball Writers Association of America's Hall of Fame ballot in 1991, his first year of eligibility.

#2777. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2775. 2. Bundesliga preview: Dynamo Dresden vs. Greuther Fürth

Dynamo Dresden will be looking to end their recent league struggles when they welcome Greuther Fürth on Friday evening, with Thomas Stamm’s side desperate for points as they look to climb away from the bottom of the 2. Bundesliga table.

The hosts head into the Matchday 11 encounter following a disappointing 2-1 defeat against Hannover 96 last weekend. Despite taking the lead through Nicolai Rapp, Dresden were unable to hold onto their advantage, with a second-half comeback leaving them bottom of the table on eight points.

Greuther Fürth, meanwhile, arrive in Saxony with renewed confidence after securing a narrow 1-0 victory over Holstein Kiel. Aaron Keller’s 87th-minute winner secured their third league victory of the campaign, moving Heiko Vogel’s side into ninth place with 12 points.

With just four points separating the two sides, Friday’s encounter presents an important opportunity for both teams to build some momentum heading into the next international break.

Dynamo Dresden have endured an inconsistent return to the second tier since promotion a few years ago and this season is no different, with two victories, two draws and six defeats from their opening ten league fixtures leaving them rooted to the foot of the table.

Stamm’s side have struggled particularly with defensive consistency, conceding 20 goals so far this season while finding the net on 12 occasions.

However, there have been encouraging signs in front of their home supporters. Dresden secured an impressive 2-0 derby victory over 1. FC Magdeburg before following that result with another 2-0 win against Schalke 04 in the DFB-Pokal.

Those performances will offer encouragement ahead of Friday’s encounter, particularly given Fürth’s own struggles for consistency this season.

The defeat against Hannover was nevertheless another frustrating setback. Dresden had looked capable of taking something from the encounter before Friedrich Müller’s dismissal allowed the hosts to take control, with the defender now unavailable for the visit of Fürth.

Stamm will therefore be demanding a response from his players, particularly in their defensive organisation and ability to maintain their intensity throughout the full 90 minutes.

Speaking ahead of the game, the Dynamo head coach acknowledged the quality of the opposition but insisted his side should approach the encounter with confidence.

“I expect a team that plays bravely with the ball and intensely against it. They resolve difficult situations with purpose. We need a really good performance, but we don’t need to hide at home.”

Stamm also stressed the importance of remaining positive, urging his players not to become frustrated if their early opportunities fail to find the back of the net.

Greuther Fürth travel to Dresden looking to build on their recent victory over Holstein Kiel, which ended a frustrating run of results and provided a welcome boost for Vogel’s side.

The visitors have collected 12 points from their opening ten league fixtures, recording three victories, three draws and four defeats. Their 13 goals scored suggest they possess some attacking quality, although 16 goals conceded highlight an area that still requires improvement.

Fürth’s biggest challenge this season has arguably been finding consistency. Their victory over Eintracht Braunschweig was followed by a disappointing 3-0 defeat against Osnabrück, before they returned to winning ways against Kiel.

The late nature of their most recent victory should nevertheless provide some confidence, with Aaron Keller finding the net in the 87th minute to secure all three points.

Vogel will be hoping his side can now register consecutive league victories for the first time this season, although he is well aware of the difficulties associated with travelling to Dresden.

The Fürth head coach has called for a better balance between defensive organisation and attacking intent, particularly after his side struggled to create opportunities in recent outings.

“Good positioning in attack is always the foundation for creating scoring opportunities. We need to be more precise in that area than we have been in recent matches.” Vogel explained ahead of the encounter.

The visitors will also be keen to avoid a repeat of their previous trip to Dresden, when they suffered a 2-0 defeat in January.

With experienced attacking players such as the league’s joint top-scorer Felix Klaus alongside the creativity of Ole Pohlmann, Fürth will certainly possess the tools to trouble their hosts if they can find the right balance going forward.

Friday’s encounter will be the 19th competitive meeting between the two sides, with Greuther Fürth holding the historical advantage.

The visitors have recorded nine victories compared to Dynamo Dresden’s four, while the remaining five encounters have ended in draws.

However, Dresden will take encouragement from their most recent meeting, which took place at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion in January 2026.

Goals from Thomas Keller and Jakob Lemmer secured a convincing 2-0 victory for the hosts, marking the beginning of an important run of results in their battle to secure survival last season.

Interestingly, that victory was Fürth’s only defeat in their previous nine meetings with Dresden, with the Franken side recording five victories and three draws during that period.

Vogel’s men will therefore be hoping to reassert their historical dominance, while Dresden will be looking to repeat their January performance and secure another important home victory.

Dynamo Dresden have several important absentees to contend with ahead of Friday’s fixture, particularly in the defensive department.

Friedrich Müller is suspended following his red card against Hannover, while Brooklyn Ezeh is also unavailable due to suspension following his dismissal for the club’s Under-21 side.

Lars Bünning and Kenneth Schmidt remain sidelined with longer-term injuries, while Thomas Keller continues to be unavailable following his concussion.

Luca Herrmann has also joined the injury list after picking up an injury against Hannover.

For Greuther Fürth, Maxim Dal remains sidelined through injury, although Vogel should otherwise have a relatively settled squad available.

#2773. Fennville volleyball's first conference championship season in 25 years ends in district final

The best season the Fennville volleyball team has had in a quarter century has come to an end.

The Blackhawks were defeated 3-0 by Grandville Calvin Christian in the Division 3 district final on Friday, Nov. 6, at Calvin Christian.

Fennville finished the season 26-12-2 and was a conference champion for the first time in 25 years.

More: Fennville's mother-daughters combo connects championship volleyball teams

More: Fennville volleyball claims first SAC division title since 2001 with huge sweep

"Not exactly how we thought our season would end," Fennville coach Rebecca Hughes said. "This is a really special team. The bond and chemistry these girls have is beyond anything I could have hoped for or imagined. They are just a great group of kids and phenomenal athletes."

Setter MacKenzie McIlwain had 12 assists, 15 digs and two kills to lead the Blackhawks, finishing her sensational career that saw her become the first player in area history to total 300 aces, 1,000 digs and 1,500 assists.

Marynn Winne finished with four kills and six digs. Adelyn Winne had five kills and two digs. MacKenzie Sabala totaled two aces, three assists and five digs and Stella Michele chipped in five digs.

"It's a tough pill to swallow but we struggled in serve receive and couldn't find a groove to get our offense going," Hughes said. "They battled the entire time and never gave up and I am so proud of them. I told them all after the game that this is the best season Fennville volleyball has had in 25 years and that's nothing to hang your heads about. It's truly something amazing they should be proud of.

"This team is going down in the record books."

The winners of the 2026 Rawlings Gold Glove were announced Sunday night by Major League Baseball and, as expected, Cubs wunderkind Pete Crow-Armstrong took home his second straight National League Gold Glove in center field. PCA, who also won a Gold Glove in 2025 and is expected to be named the NL MVP in 2026, was the best defender in baseball this past season based on both the numbers and the eye test.

Here are the game's best defenders in 2026 according to Statcast's Fielding Runs Value, an all-encompassing metric that factors in range and arm, as well as blocking and framing for catchers:

Crow-Armstrong's +26 FRV is the fifth best in a single season since FRV launched in 2016 and the second best by a non-catcher, trailing only Nick Ahmed's +28 FRV season at shortstop in 2018.

Gold Gloves have be awarded since 1957 and are given to the best defensive player at each position in each league. That first year was one MLB-wide honor at each position. In 1958, Gold Gloves were split into AL and NL. Also, it used to be three outfielders per league regardless of exact position. Now the outfield spots are broken down into left field, center field, and right field.

Winners are determined through manager/coach voting (75%) and a statistical component (25%). Team employees can not vote for their own players.

While MLB announced "finalists" for each Gold Glove a few weeks back, remember that the voting was already complete and those finalists were simply the top three vote-getters at each position. This means, obviously, that postseason performance had no impact. Here now are the 2026 Gold Glove winners.

Brandon Valenzuela (Blue Jays) and Austin Wells (Yankees)

#2769. Dynasty continues: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake wins 24th straight Section 2 girls' volleyball title

SARATOGA SPRINGS - For 23 consecutive seasons, Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake girls' volleyball coach Gary Bynon watched his players rush each other on the court and celebrate capturing a Section 2 title.

On Friday evening, Bynon looked on for a 24th time in as many seasons as his top-seeded Spartans swept No. 2 Bethlehem, 25-20, 25-16, 25-13, to claim the Class AA title at Saratoga Springs High School.

"These are young kids," Bynon said. "Every team has their own championship. I told them today that before we went out. I said, 'Listen, we're not here to repeat history. We're here to make it,' because this is theirs. It's not mine."

Burnt Hills, ranked third in the state Class AA poll, captured its 31st championship overall.

"This group is such an amazing team together," Burnt Hills junior outside hitter Alex Wemyss said. "I've never felt so close to a team in my life I don't think. We're all just best friends. We're all so young and I think we're all still developing. Every practice, every game, we're just getting better."

Burnt Hills junior setter Leah Vaughan delivered 33 assists, and eighth grader Ella Tassone added 13 kills and five digs. Bethlehem senior setter Mae Walston provided 18 assists and sophomore Madelyn Palmer totaled seven kills.

Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Bethlehem for the Section 2, Class AA title on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union)

Burnt Hills trailed by five points on three separate occasions in the opening set. Facing an 18-13 deficit, the Spartans used an 8-0 run to regain control. Wemyss totaled seven service points in the spurt and served up a blistering ace to level the set, 18-18.

"It's so exciting being on this court and being in this gym with all these people," Wemyss said. "I think it's so great to come back from that with a team like this, especially in the sectionals, because (Bethlehem) is so amazing."

"You can't make up five points in one serve, but you've got to score that one and then you've got to score another one," Bynon added. I thought that (Wemyss') big serves gave us that momentum. (Bethlehem is) such a good team and for us to be able to do that was a great thing."

Wemyss has been tremendous all season for Burnt Hills, but she played a crucial role in the Spartans weathering the storm in the first set as well as the remainder of the match.

Wemyss finished Friday's match with 16 kills, nine digs, and four aces.

"I think she's one of the top six rotation (outside hitters) in this area," Bynon said. "You can see she's a competitor. When the lights are on in the big stage, you want her on your team."

Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Bethlehem for the Section 2, Class AA title on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union)

Assists that Vaughan has recorded in her outstanding career.

Digs recorded by Burnt Hills senior libero Audri Chamberlain.

Kills registered by Eagles sophomore Brynn Sollien.

The Spartans (17-1 overall) will host the Section 3 winner in a regional final at 5 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 13.

The Eagles wrapped up an outstanding season at 15-4.

#2764. Seahawks release RB Velus Jones Jr., clear spot on active roster

Although the Seattle Seahawks remain in the midst of an injury crisis ahead of their crucial Week 9 clash against their division rival Arizona Cardinals, they'll have some some room to work with after Friday's roster shuffle.

The team announced they released running back Velus Jones Jr. and subsequently re-signed him to their practice squad, where they had a vacant spot. As a vested veteran, he was not subject to waivers.

With Jones Jr. reverting to the practice squad, Seattle now has an open spot on their 53-man roster.

Through three games, Jones Jr. logged 28 yards on nine carries, but suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 7 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs and was forced to miss Monday's game against the Chicago Bears.

Although he practiced in a limited capacity on both Wednesday and Thursday, the return of running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet on top of the team already committed to Emanuel Wilson as well as George Holani likely would've made him odd man out even if he was deemed healthy enough to return.

With DT Leonard Williams (stinger), OG Quenton Nelson (knee), WR Rashid Shaheed (knee), LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps, ribs), Brandon Pili (back), and OT Charles Cross (ankle) already ruled out, the Seahawks appear poised to fill the vacant spot with a player of one of those seven positions and they'll have plenty of options to choose from.

While WR Montorie Foster Jr. was elevated against the Bears, Seattle signed QB Adrian Martinez and linebacker Jamie Sheriff to their practice squad on Wednesday, seemingly hinting one of them could take the final spot.

Alongside Nwosu's injury, LB Connor O'Toole (foot) is deemed questionable and if he's ultimately ruled out, Sheriff fits the bill especially given his experience with the team. However, the Seahawks are currently poised to have just two quarterbacks (Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe) on the roster for Sunday's game, so it wouldn't be surprising if the opted to add a third, considering Milroe's inexperience.

The Seahawks are set to announce their game elevations on Saturday afternoon.

#2762. MLB Power Rankings: Brewers end 2026 season at No. 1 as World Series champions

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I'm done. No more. Enough is enough. I have doubted the Brewers far too many times and I decided in early August to never do it again. I started picking them to win the World Series every chance I got. I was finally right.

Every time they traded away someone good (the latest being Freddy Peralta last offseason), I thought, "OK, now is when it finally catches up with them." Only it never does. I thought they needed Tarik Skubal, both to reinforce their rotation and also to keep him away from the Dodgers. It didn't matter. They beat him and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS.

It's a juggernaut of an organization. They churn out talent and get the most out of every player they have. They seem to trade away talent at the exact right time. They develop young stars better than anyone. There's another one coming in Jesús Made, but there's no reason for Brewers fans to dream about the future when the present is World Series champions.

Jackson Chourio is becoming a superstar, Jacob Misiorowski is going to win the National League Cy Young and Christian Yelich is a former MVP, but it isn't really about the big names with this group. It's everything. It's the entire team making this train run, working as a cohesive unit. It's Robert Gasser going out and dealing in Game 3 after starting the season in the minors. It's Jake Bauers winning NLCS MVP not too long after he was ready to retire from baseball. It's Aaron Ashby putting up one of the greatest reliever performances in playoff history. It's Sal Frelick hitting a game-tying bomb. It's Cooper Pratt's coming-out party in the World Series. And on and on and on we could go.

Milwaukee is the best organization in baseball now, supplanting the former two-time defending champion Dodgers.

The Brewers head to next season with plenty of question marks, but they'll answer them. They always do. They are the champions of Major League Baseball and they sit atop the final 2026 Power Rankings.

Looking forward to next spring, my expectation is the Brewers will be No. 1. Some years, I write about why the defending champion is not No. 1. I've long since learned my lesson with this team, though. No more. The Brewers will be No. 1 heading into spring training.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2758. Colts rookie LB CJ Allen will be handling important defensive duty on Sunday for first time

Indianapolis Colts rookie starting linebacker CJ Allen, who was originally a top candidate to don the infamous green dot during training camp, will assume such duties for the first time in his NFL career on Sunday at home against the Dallas Cowboys.

As starting veteran linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) was already ruled out, the green dot duties at the 2nd level of the Indy defense will now transition to Allen, who at MIKE, will be making his 2nd career NFL start.

With Davis-Gaither unlikely to be re-signed as a veteran free agent at year-end, it's quite possible that the Colts will let Allen don the defense's lone built-in radio speaker and handle communicating the defensive play-calling to his on-the-field Indianapolis teammates the rest of the way.

There'd be no real reason not to, unless it goes poorly.

Allen was one of the few silver linings during last Sunday's blowout road loss the Jacksonville Jaguars, recording a team-high 10 tackles to go along with a sack. He projects to be a potential key piece to the Colts defensive core if he can continue to improve and develop after such an encouraging debut start last weekend.

That being said, he'll be handling an important job duty, and one that was already the center of an unnecessarily self-inflicted controversy to start the Colts' disappointing 2026 season—as veteran safety Cam Bynum initially handled green dot duties in the Colts Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.

There was a number of breakdowns and Colts defensive players being out of position, as Bynum was forced to run from down the field and the backend of the Indy secondary to relay the defensive play-calling to his teammates, which didn't provide them as much opportunity to communicate and get set pre-snap. At that time, the Colts were the only team not to use a linebacker for handling green dot duties, and it cost them in Week 1.

Here's hoping Allen's green dot debut goes a lot smoother!

#2755. Tarik Skubal landing spots: Predicting new home for two-time Cy Young winner, the offseason's best free agent

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Arguably the best pitcher in baseball is up for grabs this winter. Tarik Skubal is a free agent for the 2026-27 MLB offseason, easily the top available on the market, and every team should be trying to earn his services. But will they? Almost certainly not.

The 29-year-old southpaw spent the first six years of his major-league career with the Detroit Tigers before being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the 2026 deadline. He won back-to-back Cy Young awards in 2024 and 2025 and earned MVP votes in both seasons. He's likely to become the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history both in total value and AAV.

Of course, the giant flashing sign floating above all of this is the expiring CBA, which will run out at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, after which the owners are expected to lock out the players until a new deal is reached. Over the summer, the league proposed limiting free agency contracts, an offer that the players' union quickly disavowed, and the owners' demand for a salary cap is the underlying throughline of every negotiation. Perhaps that means Skubal will rush to sign on the dotted line before new rules are in place. Perhaps that means teams will wait out the negotiations until they know how much they have to spend -- and how they'll be punished if they do so.

Regardless, CBS Sports' MLB experts, three people who are very much not involved in contract negotiations, have gathered to predict where Skubal lands by the time Opening Day rolls around.

Mike Axisa: I'll go off the board a bit and say the Padres. The new ownership group didn't pay $3.9 billion for the franchise only to cheap out in their first offseason. They're moneyed and motivated, and that's usually enough to land the top free agents. It should appeal to Skubal too. The Padres are in the postseason most years, they play in a great (and largely pitcher-friendly) ballpark, and it's San Diego. How can you not love San Diego? Skubal to the Padres because the new owners want to make a big splash in their first offseason. That's my prediction.

Dayn Perry: I'll say the Mets top all offers by a margin sufficient to overcome their lack of appeal compared to the usual suspects (meaning, mostly, the Dodgers). They definitely need a stabilizing force in the rotation outside of Nolan McLean, and they also need a vibes shift after the deeply disappointing 2026 campaign. Landing the biggest fish of all on the market would provide all that and meet a clear need. The Mets will already be rebound candidates in 2027, and signing the likes of Skubal would position them as contenders. Obviously, the structure of the next CBA has bearing here, but maybe this all comes together before the lockout shuts it all down for an indeterminate period of time.

Matt Snyder: I'll go with the easy and obvious answer and say the Dodgers. I don't think the owners win the fight for a salary cap, but there'll be enough push from the Dodgers' end before the CBA talks shut down free agency to snatch up all the talent they can to get his contract grandfathered before a new agreement.

André Onana saved Igor Matanović's powerful header from Vincenzo Grifo's corner-kick delivery, but the rebound fell kindly to Lukas Kübler as the all-rounder scored his fifth European goal with a simple finish.
